sections.commitments:
- All code, properties and adapters under MIT.
- We maintain the pack for 12 months after the last milestone at no further cost. Everything's own contracts run it in CI, so we keep it working for ourselves.
- Every new property ships with a seeded mutant that proves it fires.
- Pinned target: at least 6 outside protocol teams running the pack in their own CI.
sections.in_scope:
- Position-based lending (Aave and Morpho style accounts) alongside loan-based markets
- Reference adapters for Uniswap V2, Morpho Blue and Euler V2, published in the repo and run in its CI
- New properties for the Euler and Cream classes: no user action leaves the caller's own position liquidatable, a donation cannot raise the value a market assigns to collateral, and a liquidatable position is always profitable to liquidate
- Echidna and Medusa entry points for every pack
- The money's main work: onboarding. An adapter guide, and hands-on help writing the adapter with each adopting team until it runs in their CI
sections.out_scope:
- Auditing any protocol, or writing a protocol's full invariant suite beyond its adapter
- Fuzzing compute or hosting
- Formal verification
- Properties specific to Everything's design (virtual reserves, its vault routing), which stay in its private suite

sections.why:
Depositors, liquidity providers and lenders on AMMs and lending markets lose money to economic logic bugs: rounding in the attacker's favour, an action that skips a health check, a share price moved by a donation, a flash loan that comes back short.

- **Euler** lost about $197 million in March 2023. A donation function skipped the health check, and the attacker then liquidated their own position ([Chainalysis](https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/euler-finance-flash-loan-attack/)).
- **Cream** lost about $130 million in October 2021 to collateral whose share price a donation had doubled ([Immunefi](https://immunefi.com/blog/bug-fix-reviews/hack-analysis-cream-finance-oct-2021/)).

Each protocol writes these checks from scratch, or skips them. Public property packs cover token standards ([crytic/properties](https://github.com/crytic/properties), [a16z/erc4626-tests](https://github.com/a16z/erc4626-tests)), not the economics of pools and markets. On this board, the Community Fuzzing RFP funds fuzzing infrastructure and the Echidna grant funds the engine; both put writing protocol invariants out of scope. This fills that gap: a team writes one adapter (10 functions for a pool, 15 for a market) and gets every property.
sections.why_grant:
- **The pack is built:** 37 properties across AMM pools (18), lending markets (17) and ERC-3156 flash lenders (2), MIT licensed. 24 generalise the invariant suite of Everything's UniPool v1 contracts; 13 are new. It already handles virtual-share markets (OpenZeppelin ERC-4626, Morpho Blue).
- **It is tested.** Three fuzz campaigns pass 16,384 calls each against reference pools. Five mutant contracts each carry one bug class (withdrawal rounding, redemption rounding, an unpaid flash fee, a flash loan repaid short, a missing health check). The fuzzer catches every one with no hints, within 35 calls, and CI checks both on every push.
- **It caught a bug nobody planted.** On its first run it flagged a stale `totalAssets` view in our own reference market, fixed before publishing.

This costs less than a from-scratch build because the property design, the adapter model and the mutant harness are finished. The money goes to the missing bug classes and to onboarding other teams.

initiative.summary: Open-source invariant properties that check the economics of AMM pools, lending markets and flash lenders under fuzzing: no withdrawal above its share, no redemption rounding in the user's favour, no healthy loan liquidated, no flash loan repaid short. 37 properties already exist, and they catch five seeded bug classes with no hints. This grant adds the bug classes behind the Euler and Cream exploits, position-based markets and Echidna and Medusa support. Its largest milestone pays only when at least 6 outside protocol teams run the pack in their own CI.
initiative.title: RA2: Economic property packs for AMMs and lending markets, fuzz tests any protocol runs in its own CI
